content.text:
Two phases are present: BaSrSmCu3O7 (mp-1227474) and Ti3PdO (mp-760414). I checked the first against a simulated pattern; the Ti3PdO peak positions are worked out from its cell, not matched point by point.

- **BaSrSmCu3O7:** The strongest pair of peaks, at about 32.1° and 32.7°, has an intensity ratio of about 57:100. Its simulated pair is at about 32.3° and 32.85° with a ratio of about 53:100. The ratio fits BaSrSmCu3O7 better than BaTmFeCuO5 (mp-1205946), which sits in nearly the same place but has the stronger peak first (100:42). The observed peaks sit about 0.15–0.2° lower than BaSrSmCu3O7's, which looks like a small cell expansion. Its predicted peak near 40.3° also accounts for the observed peak at about 40.1°.
- **Ti3PdO:** BaSrSmCu3O7 cannot explain a strong peak at about 37.6° (85% of the maximum), because it only predicts about 14% there. Peaks at about 30.2°, 31.0°, 36.3°, 37.6°, 42.15° and 44.35° match Ti3PdO's expected peaks (30.5°, 31.3°, 36.7°, 37.9°, 42.6°, 44.8°) if its cell is about 1% larger. The relative heights also fit (observed about 17, 23, 11, 85, 26, 34 against simulated about 19, 15, 10, 100, 25, 36).

I did not simulate the other five candidates. The simulated Na2BiO3 (mp-777964) pattern did not fit.

{"present": ["mp-1227474", "mp-760414"], "confidence": 0.8, "note": "The 32.1/32.7 degree pair (about 57:100) and the 40.1 degree peak match BaSrSmCu3O7, and the strong 37.6 degree peak plus the 30.2, 31.0, 42.15 and 44.35 degree peaks match Ti3PdO with a cell about 1% larger."}
